cases.reason: The quotient-ring operation is a genuine ingredient. The parent adds specified ideals, extension maps or additional properties; those data are not equivalent to a generic quotient.

reviewed_parents.source_excerpt: For a commutative ring R and ideal I, its I-adic completion R^ is the inverse limit of the quotient rings R/I^n over positive integers n, with transition maps given by reduction modulo smaller powers.
For a field k and irreducible polynomial f in k[x], the quotient k[x]/(f) is a field extending k, obtained by adjoining the class of x as a root of f.
For a prime integer p, the finite prime field F_p is the quotient field Z/(p), whose elements are integer residue classes modulo p with operations inherited from integers.
An R-module M is flat if and only if Tor_1^R(M,R/I)=0 for every finitely generated ideal I⊆R; equivalently, Tor_i^R(M,N)=0 for all R-modules N and every i>0.
A commutative ring R is Nagata if it is Noetherian and R/p is Japanese (N-2) for each prime ideal p of R.
A ring homomorphism R→S is formally unramified if, for every R-algebra A and square-zero ideal I⊆A, any R-algebra map S→A/I admits at most one lift to an R-algebra map S→A.
A closed subscheme of the affine scheme Spec(R) is a scheme isomorphic over Spec(R) to Spec(R/I) for some ideal I⊆R, equipped with the closed immersion induced by the quotient map R→R/I.
A ring map R→S is formally étale if for every R-algebra A and ideal I⊆A with I²=0, every R-algebra map S→A/I lifts to exactly one R-algebra map S→A.
A finite-type algebra S over a field k is a global complete intersection if some presentation S≅k[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_c) satisfies dim(S)=n−c.
For a Noetherian commutative ring R and ideal I, the I-adic completion R^ is the inverse-limit ring lim_n R/I^n, with structure homomorphism R→R^ induced by the quotient maps.
A commutative ring homomorphism R→S is formally smooth if every R-algebra map S→A/I lifts to an R-algebra map S→A whenever A is an R-algebra and I⊆A satisfies I²=0.
A ring map R→S is a relative global complete intersection if S admits a presentation R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_c) for which every nonempty fibre of Spec(S)→Spec(R) has dimension n−c.
A ring map R→S is of finite presentation if S is R-isomorphic to R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_m) for finite families of polynomial generators and relations.

A field extension K/k is formally smooth over k when every k-algebra map K→A/I across a square-zero quotient lifts to A. In positive characteristic this is equivalent to separability of K/k; in characteristic zero every field extension satisfies it.
A local ring (R,m) is complete if the canonical homomorphism R→lim_n R/m^n is an isomorphism; equivalently, its m-adic completion introduces no new elements.

Let R→S be a homomorphism of commutative rings. For a prime ideal q⊆S with contraction p=q∩R, the local ring of the fibre at q is S_q/pS_q. Equivalently, it is the localization of the fibre ring S⊗_Rκ(p) at the prime corresponding to q.

cases.reason: The formal polynomial algebra is a genuine ingredient. Evaluated polynomial values, chosen maps and generator/relations data remain separate.

reviewed_parents.source_excerpt: A family (x_i) of elements of a field extension K/k is algebraically independent over k when the evaluation homomorphism k[X_i:i∈I]→K, sending each indeterminate X_i to x_i, is injective.

For a ring map R→S, let P=R[X_s:s∈S] map canonically onto S and put I=ker(P→S). The naive cotangent complex NL_{S/R} is the two-term complex I/I²→Ω_{P/R}⊗_P S, with I/I² in homological degree 1 and the induced differential from universal derivation.
The characteristic polynomial of an n×n matrix A over a commutative ring R is the polynomial χ_A(t)=det(t I_n−A) in R[t], where I_n denotes the identity matrix.
An extension K/k of fields is algebraic if every element α∈K satisfies a nonzero polynomial with coefficients in k.

For an R-module M and elements f_1,…,f_c generating J⊆R, the sequence is M-quasi-regular if the graded map (M/JM)⊗_{R/J}(R/J)[X_1,…,X_c]→⊕_{n≥0}J^nM/J^{n+1}M, sending X_i to the class of f_i, is an isomorphism.
A finite-type algebra S over a field k is a global complete intersection if some presentation S≅k[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_c) satisfies dim(S)=n−c.
A ring map R→S is a relative global complete intersection if S admits a presentation R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_c) for which every nonempty fibre of Spec(S)→Spec(R) has dimension n−c.
An element α of a field extension E/F is algebraic over F if some nonzero polynomial f∈F[x] satisfies f(α)=0.
A field extension E/F is algebraic if every element of E satisfies at least one nonzero polynomial with coefficients in F.
A ring map R→S is of finite presentation if S is R-isomorphic to R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_m) for finite families of polynomial generators and relations.
A ring map R→S is of finite type if S can be generated as an R-algebra by finitely many elements, equivalently S is a quotient of R[x_1,…,x_n] for some finite n.
Polynomials f,g∈k[x] over a field k are relatively prime when the ideal (f,g) they generate is the entire polynomial ring k[x].

Let R be a commutative ring with multiplicative identity and let P=∑_{k=0}^n a_kX^k∈R[X] be nonzero. Its degree deg(P) is the greatest integer k≥0 for which a_k≠0_R. This definition does not assign a finite degree to the zero polynomial.

Let R⊆S be an inclusion of commutative rings with identity, and let x∈S. The element x is strongly transcendental over R if for every integer n≥0, coefficients a_0,…,a_n∈R, and u∈S, the equation u(a_0+a_1x+⋯+a_nx^n)=0 implies ua_i=0 for every i=0,…,n.

cases.reason: Ideal multiplication can be defined in nonunital rings for positive powers; the candidate currently requires commutative unital coefficients, potentially narrower than the nilpotent-ideal parent.

reviewed_parents.source_excerpt: An ideal I of a ring R is nilpotent when there is a single positive integer n for which the product ideal I^n is the zero ideal.

An integral domain R is a Dedekind domain in this factorization characterization if every nonzero ideal factors as a finite product of nonzero prime ideals and this decomposition is unique up to permuting the factors.
Equivalently, an ideal I⊆R is pure when I∩J=IJ for every ideal J of R; it is enough to test finitely generated ideals J.
For a Noetherian commutative ring R and ideal I, the I-adic completion R^ is the inverse-limit ring lim_n R/I^n, with structure homomorphism R→R^ induced by the quotient maps.
Given an ideal I of a commutative ring R, the Rees algebra of I is the nonnegatively graded R-algebra ⊕_{n≥0}I^n, with I^0=R and multiplication induced by the products I^m I^n⊆I^{m+n}.
For a prime ideal p of a commutative ring R and n≥0, the nth symbolic power p^(n) is the contraction to R of p^n R_p, equivalently the kernel of R→R_p/p^nR_p.

cases.reason: Candidate context quantifies over all real times. A single-variable integrability requirement or integer-indexed process does not entail that condition.

reviewed_parents.source_excerpt: For an integrable real random variable X on (Ω,F,P) and a sub-σ-algebra G⊆F, a version of E[X|G] is an integrable G-measurable random variable Z satisfying ∫_A Z dP = ∫_A X dP for every A∈G.
A real-valued process (X_t)_{t≥0} adapted to a filtration (F_t)_{t≥0}, with E|X_t|<∞ for every t≥0, is a martingale if E[X_t|F_s]=X_s almost surely whenever 0≤s≤t.
A real-valued discrete-time process (X_n)_{n≥0}, adapted to a filtration (F_n)_{n≥0} and satisfying E|X_n|<∞ for every n, is a martingale if E[X_{n+1}|F_n]=X_n almost surely for each n≥0.
An integrable adapted real-valued discrete-time process (X_n,F_n)_{n≥0} is a martingale if E[X_m|F_n]=X_n almost surely whenever 0≤n≤m are integers.

cases.reason: Candidate context restricts U to Spec(R), whereas connectedness parents quantify over clopen subsets in arbitrary topological spaces.

reviewed_parents.source_excerpt: For a commutative ring R, a subset U of Spec(R) is simultaneously open and closed exactly when there is an idempotent e of R (so e²=e) such that U=D(e)={p in Spec(R):e is not in p}; this e is unique.
A nonempty topological space X is connected if it cannot be expressed as a disjoint union of two nonempty open subsets; equivalently its only clopen subsets are ∅ and X.
A topological space (X,τ) is connected if every subset C⊆X that is both open and closed in X satisfies C=∅ or C=X.
A topological space X is connected precisely when its only subsets that are both open and closed are ∅ and X.

reviewed_parents.source_excerpt: For a field k and irreducible polynomial f in k[x], the quotient k[x]/(f) is a field extending k, obtained by adjoining the class of x as a root of f.
A field K is algebraically closed precisely when it has no proper algebraic field extension; equivalently, each nonconstant one-variable polynomial with coefficients in K admits a root in K.
For a nonconstant polynomial P over a field F, a splitting field is a field extension E/F in which P factors into linear terms and which is generated over F by all its roots.
The separable degree of an irreducible polynomial f over F is the number of its distinct roots in an algebraic closure of F, counted without multiplicities.

reviewed_parents.source_excerpt: An R-module M is finitely generated if there exist m_1,…,m_n∈M such that M=Rm_1+⋯+Rm_n; equivalently there is a surjective homomorphism R^n→M for some finite n.
The colimit of a diagram (M_i,μ_ij) of R-modules is the quotient of the direct sum ⊕_i M_i by the submodule generated by all elements ι_i(m)−ι_j(μ_ij(m)) for i≤j.
An R-module M is finitely generated if a finite list m_1,…,m_n generates all of M by R-linear combinations; equivalently there is an R-linear surjection R^n→M.
